name: Marcus T.
text: Finally someone said it! I've been teaching my students to sing intervals first for years and it makes such a difference. They actually understand what a third sounds like instead of just memorizing numbers.

name: Rebecca K.
text: This is interesting but how do you manage this with larger classes? I teach 30+ students and getting everyone to sing intervals accurately before naming them seems time-consuming.

name: David P.
text: I tried this approach last semester and my students' ear training improved noticeably. Highly recommend giving it a shot even if it feels slower at first.

name: Sophie M.
text: Does anyone else teach singing intervals using hand signs first? I find that combining kinesthetic, aural, and then visual/naming creates the strongest connections.

name: James H.
text: Skipping singing is definitely a mistake I made early in my teaching. My college theory students struggle with intervals specifically because they never developed that intuitive sound memory.
